prevention.title: Wear a Well-Fitted Mask
prevention.desc: Wear a high-filtration mask (N95, FFP2, or well-fitted surgical mask) in crowded, enclosed, or poorly ventilated public spaces to filter airborne droplets.
prevention.source: WHO Infection Prevention and Control Guidance

prevention.title: Improve Indoor Ventilation
prevention.desc: Open windows and doors to increase natural airflow, or use air purifiers with HEPA filtration when gathering indoors.
prevention.source: WHO Roadmap to improve and ensure good indoor ventilation in COVID-19 context

prevention.title: Practice Regular Hand Hygiene
prevention.desc: Wash hands frequently with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, or use an alcohol-based hand rub with at least 60% alcohol.

prevention.title: Maintain Physical Distance
prevention.desc: Keep a physical distance of at least 1 metre (3 feet) from others, especially from individuals showing respiratory symptoms such as coughing or sneezing.

prevention.title: Self-Isolate When Unwell
prevention.desc: If you experience fever, cough, fatigue, or other symptoms, stay home, separate yourself from household members, and seek medical consultation.

emergency.name: Difficulty Breathing or Shortness of Breath
Persistent Pain or Pressure in the Chest
emergency.action: Call an ambulance or visit the nearest emergency department immediately.

emergency.name: Confusion or Inability to Stay Awake
Pale, Gray, or Blue-Colored Skin, Lips, or Nail Beds
emergency.action: Sign of hypoxemia — seek emergency oxygen therapy.

vaccination.title: Primary Vaccination Series
vaccination.summary: Protects against severe illness, hospitalization, and death caused by SARS-CoV-2. Approved vaccines stimulate the immune system to produce antibodies and T-cell responses.
vaccination.details: Most vaccines require 2 primary doses spaced 3 to 12 weeks apart depending on vaccine platform (mRNA, viral vector, or protein subunit).
vaccination.source: WHO Strategic Advisory Group of Experts (SAGE) Roadmap

vaccination.title: Precautionary / Booster Doses
vaccination.summary: Restores waning immunity, particularly for older adults, healthcare personnel, and individuals with underlying comorbidities.
vaccination.details: Updated formulations (bivalent or XBB variant-adapted) offer broader cross-neutralization against evolving sub-lineages.
vaccination.source: MoHFW National COVID-19 Vaccination Operational Guidelines

vaccination.title: Safety & Adverse Events Monitoring
vaccination.summary: Vaccines undergo extensive pre-clinical trials and continuous pharmacovigilance across billions of administered doses.
vaccination.details: Common side effects include mild fever, headache, muscle soreness, and injection site tenderness, typically resolving within 48 hours.

myths.myth: COVID-19 is just a common cold or influenza.
myths.fact: COVID-19 is caused by SARS-CoV-2, which has a higher mortality rate, higher transmissibility, and can cause systemic complications including multi-organ failure and Long COVID.

myths.myth: Vaccines cause COVID-19 infection or alter human DNA.
myths.fact: COVID-19 vaccines do not contain live virus that can reproduce inside human cells, and mRNA vaccines never enter the nucleus of the cell where DNA is kept.
myths.source: WHO Science in 5: Vaccines and DNA

myths.myth: Antibiotics can prevent or treat COVID-19.
myths.fact: Antibiotics kill bacteria, not viruses. COVID-19 is viral. Antibiotics should only be prescribed if a secondary bacterial co-infection is diagnosed by a physician.

myths.myth: Hot weather or drinking warm water prevents COVID-19 transmission.
myths.fact: You can catch COVID-19 no matter how sunny or hot the weather is. Countries with hot climates have documented high case volumes without environmental immunity.

myths.myth: Holding your breath for 10 seconds without coughing proves you don't have COVID-19.
myths.fact: Being able to hold your breath does not mean you are free from coronavirus or any other lung disease. A confirmed diagnosis requires laboratory testing (RT-PCR or Rapid Antigen).

helplines.name: National Health Helpline (India)
helplines.desc: Toll-free national COVID-19 helpline for healthcare queries, guidance, and teleconsultation referrals.
helplines.source: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), Govt of India

helplines.name: Central Health Ministry Control Room
helplines.desc: Direct telephone line for emergency escalation and central health query coordination.

helplines.name: National Childline Helpline
helplines.desc: Emergency assistance for children in distress or affected by pandemic-related family emergencies.
helplines.source: Ministry of Women and Child Development

helplines.name: Tele-MANAS Mental Health Assistance
helplines.desc: National tele-mental health programme providing psychological support, counseling, and distress relief.
